target_moa.text: Vibegron is a selective human beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist; activation of the beta-3 adrenergic receptor increases bladder capacity by relaxing the detrusor smooth muscle during bladder filling.

citations.quote: Vibegron is a selective human beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist. Activation of the beta-3 adrenergic receptor increases bladder capacity by relaxing the detrusor smooth muscle during bladder filling.

Vibegron (RVT-901, URO-901, MK-4618, KRP-114V), a new molecular entity (NME), is a selective agonist of the human beta-3 adrenergic receptor (\beta 3-AR), developed for treatment of overactive bladder (OAB) with 75 mg oral daily dosage.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>2%) were headache (4.0% vs 2.4% placebo), urinary tract infection, nasopharyngitis (2.8% vs 1.7%), diarrhea (2.2% vs 1.1%), nausea (2.2% vs 1.1%), and upper respiratory tract infection (2.0% vs 0.7%). Urinary retention is the identified warning.

Urinary retention has been reported in patients taking GEMTESA. The risk of urinary retention may be increased in patients with bladder outlet obstruction and also in patients taking muscarinic antagonist medications for the treatment of OAB.
